projects.title: Atlas.AI — Production-Grade Multi-Agent Research System (MARS)
projects.tagline: Production-grade 9-node LangGraph multi-agent research system with RAG, 4-provider fallback & AWS EC2 deployment

caseStudy.overview: Atlas.AI is a production-grade multi-agent autonomous research system featuring a 9-node LangGraph pipeline, self-correcting critique loops, and 6 specialized academic AI agents. Deployed across a 6-service multi-cloud architecture (AWS EC2 for the AI engine, Vercel, Qdrant Cloud, Supabase, Upstash Redis, MongoDB Atlas), it automates deep academic research, fact verification, and report synthesis while reducing zero-output failures to <0.5%.
caseStudy.problem: Overcome LLM hallucinations, single-prompt shallowness, and API timeout failures by building an autonomous multi-agent pipeline with self-correcting critique loops, 4-provider LLM fallback cascades, high-accuracy RAG vector retrieval, and async SSE streaming.
responsibilities: Architecting the 9-node LangGraph multi-agent pipeline with self-correcting rewrite loops
Deploying the Python/FastAPI AI engine on AWS EC2 with systemd and reverse proxy
Engineering a TypeScript Node.js/Express API gateway with dual-token JWT authentication (15-min access + 7-day refresh rotation)
Implementing Upstash Redis caching (<50ms response) and asynchronous SSE job queues across 8 route modules
Building 6 specialized academic AI Agents with Qdrant vector vault RAG (+38% factual accuracy)
Configuring 4-provider AI fallback cascade (Mistral → Groq → Gemini → OpenRouter) reducing failures to <0.5%
Developing interactive Next.js 15 / React 19 workspace with real-time SSE streaming and LangGraph visualizer
Orchestrating 6-service multi-cloud stack across AWS EC2, Vercel, Qdrant Cloud, Supabase, Upstash, and MongoDB Atlas

frontend.description: Interactive Next.js 15 and React 19 research workspace featuring real-time Server-Sent Events (SSE), custom LangGraph workflow visualization, live agent execution tracking, automated report scoring, and analytics dashboards.

apiGateway.description: Node.js/Express TypeScript API gateway with dual-token JWT auth (15-min access + 7-day refresh rotation), Upstash Redis caching (<50ms response vs 90+ second pipeline runs), CSRF protection, and an async SSE job queue eliminating HTTP gateway timeouts across 8 route modules.

aiOrchestrationEngine.description: Python/FastAPI AI engine deployed on AWS EC2, executing the 9-node LangGraph multi-agent pipeline with a 4-provider fallback cascade (Mistral → Groq → Gemini → OpenRouter) and Qdrant Cloud vector vault RAG.

multiAgentPipeline.role: Performs autonomous query expansion and breaks research topics into targeted sub-questions.
Conducts intelligent web intelligence gathering via Tavily API across verified scientific and web sources.
Scrapes and cleans unstructured web content, filtering ads, navigation, and noise.
Extracts and condenses key data points into structured factual summaries.
Generates dense embeddings via FastEmbed, stores them in Qdrant Cloud, and retrieves relevant semantic chunks (+38% factual gain).
Synthesizes comprehensive research reports using Mistral Large with structured citation references.
Cross-verifies claims against raw retrieved sources to identify and eliminate hallucinations.
Evaluates report quality (>92% average critique score); triggers automated rewrite cycles if score < 8/10.
Extracts entity-relationship networks for dynamic concept map rendering in the frontend.

specializedAcademicAgents.description: Generates cross-examination questions and stress-tests academic arguments against counter-evidence.

specializedAcademicAgents.name: Temporal Fact-Checker

specializedAcademicAgents.description: Provides Academic, Concise, Casual, and Technical rewrite modes with semantic integrity.

Deploys Next.js 15 frontend and serverless edge API gateway.
Manages high-dimensional vector vault for semantic RAG retrieval.
Stores historical research analytics, session tracking, and workflow logs.
Provides sub-50ms query caching and rate limiting across gateway modules.
Handles user credentials, profile records, and subscription billing.

Upstash Redis sub-50ms query caching eliminating redundant LLM pipeline runs
4-provider fallback cascade cutting downtime and zero-output failures to <0.5%

caseStudy.outcome: A production-grade, 6-service multi-cloud research system achieving an 85.7% pass rate across 28 automated E2E tests, >92% average critique score, and sub-50ms cached responses — powered by AWS EC2, Next.js 15, LangGraph, and Qdrant.

projects.title: Studio Butterfly AI Support Agent
projects.tagline: Autonomous AI support agent with RAG, tool calling, and stateful memory (local project)

caseStudy.overview: A production-grade, autonomous decision-making AI support agent capable of answering general queries, retrieving info from uploaded documents (RAG), and using mock tool calling for product/order details — built to automate and improve customer support accuracy.

systemWorkflow: User message + chat history sent to Mistral LLM
LLM decides if a tool call is needed; fetches from local JSON databases if so
If document context is needed, searches Qdrant Vector DB for relevant chunks
If Qdrant confidence score is below 0.65, a fallback 'not found' message is triggered
Conversation saved in memory and displayed in real-time on the frontend

backend: Activate venv (.venv\Scripts\Activate.ps1 on Windows / source .venv/bin/activate on macOS/Linux)
Create .env with MISTRAL_API_KEY, MISTRAL_CHAT_MODEL, MISTRAL_EMBED_MODEL, QDRANT_URL, QDRANT_COLLECTION_NAME

testScenarios: Memory Test: tell the agent your name, then ask 'What is my name?'
Product Search: 'Do you have a wireless mouse?'
Order Status: 'Where is my order ORD001?'
Document RAG: upload a PDF and ask questions about its content

keyFeatures.name: Autonomous Routing
keyFeatures.description: AI decides whether to give a general response, call a tool, or use RAG based on the user's message.

keyFeatures.name: Tool Calling
keyFeatures.description: Fetches real-time mock data (orders.json, products.json) for order status or product pricing queries.

keyFeatures.name: RAG - Document Analysis
keyFeatures.description: Users upload PDF/Text files; AI extracts context to answer accurately.

keyFeatures.name: Stateful Memory
keyFeatures.description: Remembers the last 10 conversation turns for fluid, multi-turn conversations.

caseStudy.outcome: By bypassing bloated frameworks like LangChain in favor of a custom agent router and lightweight Qdrant Vector DB, the agent is exceptionally fast and scalable for automating real-time customer support.

projects.title: AI Career Assistant (RAG + LLM Platform)
projects.tagline: AI-powered platform for Resume Generation, Job Description Matching, and Interview Preparation

caseStudy.overview: Built a full-stack AI Career Assistant using Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) and Large Language Models (LLMs). The platform enables users to generate ATS-friendly resumes, optimize CVs based on job descriptions, prepare for interviews with AI-generated questions, and chat with their uploaded career documents using context-aware responses.
targetUsers: Students and fresh graduates applying for internships and jobs
Professionals tailoring CVs to specific job descriptions
Candidates preparing for technical and HR interviews
solutionApproach: Users upload resumes, job descriptions, or career-related documents.
Documents are parsed, chunked, embedded, and stored in a vector database.
The system retrieves relevant context using semantic similarity search.
LLMs generate ATS-friendly resumes, resume improvements, interview questions, and personalized answers using retrieved context.
Responses are streamed to the frontend with supporting document references.
keyFeatures: Resume optimization based on Job Description
Technical and HR interview question generation
Resume analysis with personalized improvement suggestions

challengesAndSolutions.problem: Resume recommendations lacked relevance.
challengesAndSolutions.solution: Used RAG to retrieve job-specific context before LLM generation.

challengesAndSolutions.problem: Large resumes and job descriptions increased response time.
challengesAndSolutions.solution: Implemented chunking, caching, and asynchronous document indexing.

challengesAndSolutions.problem: Hallucinated interview answers.
challengesAndSolutions.solution: Grounded prompts with retrieved resume and job description context.

challengesAndSolutions.problem: Poor semantic retrieval.
challengesAndSolutions.solution: Optimized chunk size, embedding models, and similarity threshold.

futureScope: AI mock interview with voice support
caseStudy.outcome: Developed a production-ready AI Career Assistant that leverages RAG and LLMs to generate ATS-friendly resumes, optimize CVs for specific job descriptions, provide personalized interview preparation, and deliver accurate, context-aware career guidance.

projects.title: Predictive Analytics for Maternal Mental Health Using Machine Learning (BDHS 2022)
projects.tagline: ML-based prediction of depression/anxiety risk factors from the Bangladesh Demographic and Health Survey 2022

caseStudy.overview: Applies advanced ML techniques to the BDHS 2022 dataset to identify and predict risk factors for depression, anxiety, and distress among women, aiming to build a robust, generalizable model for early screening and targeted intervention.

solutionApproach.dataLeakagePrevention: Correlation analysis and single-feature testing identified variables like MTH22 (months since last birth) as perfect separators reflecting survey timing rather than real risk; these were excluded to ensure generalization.
solutionApproach.featureSelection: Combined union of Mutual Information (MI), Chi-Square, and Random Forest importance, applied on the original training data.
solutionApproach.classImbalanceHandling: SMOTE (Synthetic Minority Over-sampling Technique) applied AFTER feature selection (not before) to avoid introducing synthetic bias.

challengesAndSolutions.name: Extreme Class Imbalance
challengesAndSolutions.description: Only 1,026 of 30,078 respondents (3.4%) tested positive for depression — standard models tend to ignore the minority class.

challengesAndSolutions.name: Data Leakage Risks
challengesAndSolutions.description: Initial models hit an unrealistic 100% accuracy, signaling severe data leakage impossible in real-world medical/psychological prediction.

results.evaluationApproach: ROC-AUC as the primary metric (due to imbalance) alongside strict monitoring of the train-vs-test accuracy gap to prevent overfitting.

figures: Feature Importance (Random Forest) — highlights age, geographic clustering, husband's education as top predictors
Model Performance Comparison — Precision, Recall, F1-Score, ROC-AUC across all six models
ROC-AUC Ranking — XGBoost highest, most reliable at distinguishing depressed vs. non-depressed cases
Train vs. Test Accuracy — gap under 5% indicates good generalization
XGBoost Confusion Matrix — best-performing model's test set results

impact: Scalable, low-cost public health screening tool using easily collectible demographic/socio-economic variables
Enables targeted resource allocation via key predictors like geographic clustering and education levels
Establishes a reproducible ML pipeline correctly handling demographic survey data nuances, setting a standard for epidemiological ML studies
caseStudy.outcome: A robust, generalizable XGBoost-based predictive model for maternal mental health risk, engineered with careful data-leakage prevention, proper feature selection ordering, and rigorous overfitting checks.

projects.title: COVID-19 Vaccine Side Effect Prediction Using Machine Learning
projects.tagline: ML-based prediction of COVID-19 vaccine side effects using real-world survey data from Bangladesh

caseStudy.overview: Developed a machine learning framework to predict the likelihood of COVID-19 vaccine side effects using demographic, health, and vaccination-related information collected from vaccinated individuals in Bangladesh. The project focuses on early risk assessment and identifying the most influential factors associated with post-vaccination side effects.

dataset.source: Primary survey dataset collected through Google Forms

methodology.dataPreprocessing: Handled missing values, encoded categorical variables, normalized numerical features, and prepared data for ML training.
methodology.featureSelection: Applied Mutual Information, Chi-Square, and Random Forest Feature Importance to identify the most influential predictors.
methodology.modelTraining: Compared multiple supervised machine learning algorithms using cross-validation and performance metrics.
methodology.evaluation: Measured Accuracy, Precision, Recall, F1-Score, ROC-AUC, and Confusion Matrix to select the best-performing model.

challengesAndSolutions.name: Real-World Survey Data Quality
challengesAndSolutions.description: Survey responses contained missing values, inconsistent entries, and categorical variables requiring preprocessing.

challengesAndSolutions.name: Feature Selection
challengesAndSolutions.description: Identifying the most relevant demographic and medical features was essential to improve model performance and reduce overfitting.

challengesAndSolutions.name: Model Generalization
challengesAndSolutions.description: Preventing overfitting while maintaining strong predictive performance across unseen data.

results.evaluationApproach: Compared multiple ML models using Accuracy, Precision, Recall, F1-Score, ROC-AUC, and Confusion Matrix while monitoring overfitting through train-test performance comparison.

keyFindings: Random Forest achieved the highest overall prediction performance.
Feature selection significantly improved model accuracy.
Previous allergic reactions, chronic diseases, age, and vaccine dose were among the strongest predictors.
The trained model demonstrated reliable performance for predicting post-vaccination side effects.

impact: Supports early identification of individuals at higher risk of vaccine side effects.
Helps healthcare professionals make data-driven vaccination recommendations.
Provides a reusable machine learning pipeline for healthcare prediction tasks.
Demonstrates practical application of predictive analytics in public health research.
caseStudy.outcome: Built a robust machine learning prediction system capable of estimating COVID-19 vaccine side-effect risk from demographic and clinical information, with Random Forest emerging as the best-performing model and providing valuable insights for healthcare decision-making.
